guessing_reference.title: Measuring Password Guessability for an Entire University
guessing_reference.locator: Section 5.1; Table 6, printed page 181 / PDF page 10
guessing_reference.attacker: public / limited-knowledge; modified Weir algorithm; no in-organization password training
guessing_reference.reported_guess_unit: paper-reported algorithm guess number; equivalence to delivered distinct verifier work is an explicit model assumption
guessing_reference.source_policy: minimum 8 characters, four character classes and dictionary check; MTcomp8 has a stronger dictionary check
guessing_reference.supports: Aggregate source-population rank anchors and sampling/selection distinctions; not a SEAMLESS or service-account probability.
guessing_reference.excluded_rows: Knowledgeable attacker, plaintext-leak subsets and already-cracked subsets are not used. The 0.05 percentage-point allowance handles printed rounding only, not sampling/transport uncertainty.

supporting_sources.supports: Guessing strategy/configuration and candidate generation cost affect rank and delivered work; no numeric endpoints transferred from this paper.

supporting_sources.locator: Recommendations: long randomly generated service passwords; AES plus strong passwords
supporting_sources.supports: Separate manually set service passwords from generated passwords; 14 characters is a recommendation. Neither a 94-symbol uniform generator nor a 25–50% manual mixture weight is asserted by Microsoft.
AS-REP etype23 and TGS etype23 are separate formats/modes; no throughput or success percentage.
RC4-HMAC password/key and encrypted-material verification semantics, not rank mass or performance.
AES string-to-key includes iteration/salt parameters; RC4 work envelope cannot be transferred to AES.
Exclusion example: company-level prevalence/success is not per-account bounded recovery probability; no numerical value used.
